decisions.reason: The geometric sums are strictly positive for every real q>1, and for xi!=1 their vanishing is equivalent to xi^n=1, so both scalar conclusions are valid without any p-adic hypothesis. The title incorrectly identified every such q as p-adic; corrected the title to the actual real affine-Hecke scope, leaving Statement and proof unchanged.

The claim that I is open in Z_3^4 is false: perturbing the upper-left entry of the identity changes its determinant. This is a nonfatal ambient-space error, repaired by closedness in compact Z_3^4 and openness relative to G from a,b,d in Z_3 and c in 3Z_3. Hence 0<mu(I)<infinity follows by the stated nonzero-Haar finite-cover argument. Checked the congruence basis, compact-group averaging, three simple cosets, tree convolution coefficients, IM basis bijection, and finite-sum smooth-vector action; no theorem hypothesis or Statement changed.

There is no logical dependency cycle. SCHEMA.md expressly makes justified_by a well-definedness discharge whose result depends on the definition via deps, and forbids the reverse deps edge; this carrier follows that rule exactly. Filtration proof 3.1 establishes centrality of A^{W_P}, explicitly separates two finite W_P-orbits by invariant Laurent polynomials, and uses scalar action of central operators on a finite-dimensional irreducible module to prove the unique orbit. It uses the raw parabolic algebra and weight definitions, never the claimed single-orbit central-character conclusion. PBW supplies the embedded lattice algebra; induction and finite generalized-weight conventions are well defined.

The cited filtration lemma explicitly proves generalized-weight exactness in proof 2.1 by polynomial projections in a finite lattice basis of commuting operators; an intermediate proved fact need not also be repeated in its Statement. These projections preserve every A-invariant subspace and descend to the quotient, proving the exact sequences used here. Together with the multiset filtration and strict norm decrease, this identifies the top space with S=1 tensor sigma. Every proper H-submodule avoids S by irreducibility and cyclic generation, so their sum stays in the fixed lower-weight space and is proper; the quotient is simple and retains S with its H_P action. P=B, empty roots and central exponents give identity induction and cause no exception. No repair is required.
